pos.personaBrief: His 1965 book rejects Brazilian possession and plans fast counters; Estudiantes ran at rivals and attacked with rehearsed moves, not ball control.

pro.personaBrief: Counter-based plan with fast transitions and rehearsed changes of flank; safe, practical ball use rather than patient build-up.

est.personaBrief: Everyone had a tactical order to fulfil (only Veron free), with rehearsed roles, marking tasks and relevos; structure over improvised combination.

lar.personaBrief: Rehearsed changes of flank, crossing wingers like Ribaudo and Conigliaro, and an overlapping full-back; wide play as a tool, with a physical midfield in the middle.

blo.personaBrief: Forwards chased rivals into their own area, plus an offside line and pressing midfield; high, aggressive block.

mar.personaBrief: Marcas personales, Bilardo taught to mark Maschio, tight marking of forwards; individual marking.

pla.personaBrief: He studied rivals, changed shirt numbers to confuse and prepared specific plays, yet kept a consistent method and imposed it on players.

res.personaBrief: Ultra-tactical, did anything to win, called an illicit association by critics; result above style.

sis.personaBrief: Drilled collective where all fulfil all functions; the only free player was Veron, a stated exception.

jog.personaBrief: Double sessions, long concentrations, runners who ran like demons, combative marking players like Pachame; physical intensity prized.

bas.personaBrief: Built Estudiantes on the Tercera que mata youngsters (Poletti, Malbernat, Pachame, Veron) and nurtured Nacional's Kinder, while winning was the aim.

lid.personaBrief: Declared he was responsible and no interference would be admitted; demanded extreme work and discipline, though he persuaded and held long talks.
